info.name: MovieE-Ticket — Prototype API Collection
info.description:
FESE209 Final Project — Movie Ticket Booking System
Team: Sivatey · Sveita · Sokhomal · Sonita
Instructor: Pen Voneat

Demonstrates:
- ADR-001: Microservices (2 independent services)
- ADR-003: MySQL for transactional booking data
- ADR-004: Redis seat-lock TTL (double-booking prevention)
- ADR-005: Async email notification after booking (SendGrid simulation)

Run order: Health Checks → Get Showtimes → Get Seats → Create Booking → Check Notifications → Double-Book Test → Cancel Booking

request.description:
Proves ADR-001: Booking Service runs independently.
Expected: { service: 'booking-service', status: 'ok' }

Proves ADR-001: Notification Service runs independently.
Expected: { service: 'notification-service', status: 'ok' }

Returns 2 seeded movies: Avengers: Doomsday and Mission Impossible 8.
Copy a showtime 'id' value to use in the next request.

Replace PASTE_SHOWTIME_ID_HERE with a showtime id from the previous request.

Returns 7 seats with status:
- available: free to book
- temporarily_held: Redis lock active (ADR-004)
- booked: confirmed booking in MySQL

Copy an 'available' seat's 'id' for the booking step.

SAD Endpoint: POST /bookings

Replace showtime_id and seat_id with values from Step 2.
payment_method options: 'ABA Pay', 'Wing', 'cash'

Proves:
- ADR-003: MySQL ACID transaction used
- ADR-004: Redis seat lock acquired before DB write
- ADR-005: Notification Service called asynchronously — email sent after this returns

Check Step 4 after this to see the email notification log.

After creating a booking, this shows the email notification that was sent asynchronously.

Proves ADR-005: The notification was logged AFTER the booking response returned.
In production, this would trigger a real SendGrid email to the user.
Notification channel is 'email' only — no SMS.

SAD Endpoint: POST /notify

Normally called by Booking Service asynchronously.
You can also call it directly to show Notification Service works independently (ADR-001).

Email channel only — simulates a SendGrid API call in production.

ADR-004 DEMO: Use the SAME showtime_id and seat_id from Step 3.

Expected response: 409 Conflict
{ 'error': 'Seat is temporarily held by another user' }

This proves the Redis TTL seat-lock is working:
SET seat_lock:{seat_id} NX EX 600
NX = only set if not exists — second request gets blocked immediately.

Returns all confirmed bookings from MySQL.
Copy a booking 'id' to use in the cancel request below.

Replace PASTE_BOOKING_ID_HERE with a booking id from Get All Bookings.

Cancels the booking, releases the seat back to available, releases Redis lock,
and asynchronously sends a cancellation email notification.
